title: Names Can Hurt: Spotting Slopsquatting Risks Caused by Package Name Hallucinations in Local Coding LLMs
abstract: arXiv:2608.23897v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: When a code generating language model fabricates a Python package name, an adversary who has pre-registered that name on PyPI can convert that hallucination into a supply chain compromise. This event has been termed as 'slopsquatting'. We propose a two layer detector to counter this issue. The first layer performs a deterministic PyPI existence check. The second is a Random Forest classifier trained on ten features derived from the package name and its PyPI metadata. An import name reconciler bridges the two, resolving cases such as 'import cv2' versus 'pip install opencv-python' without a security bypass. The detector is embedded in a LangGraph state machine that retries at escalating temperatures and, on repeated failure, routes to a stronger fallback model. translated_title: 名字可能带来伤害：识别本地编码大语言模型中由包名幻觉引发的Slopsquatting风险
translated_abstract: 当代码生成语言模型虚构出一个Python包名时，预先在PyPI上注册该名称的攻击者可将此幻觉转化为供应链攻击。这一事件被称为“slopsquatting”。我们提出一个两层检测器来解决此问题。第一层执行确定性的PyPI存在性检查。第二层是一个随机森林分类器，基于从包名及其PyPI元数据中提取的十个特征进行训练。一个导入名协调器桥接两层，解决诸如“import cv2”与“pip install opencv-python”之间的映射，而无需安全绕过。该检测器嵌入在LangGraph状态机中，以递增温度进行重试，并在反复失败后路由到更强的回退模型。在300个精选提示中，该管道在76%的运行中产生无幻觉代码。主模型在28.7%的情况下耗尽重试预算；模型内重试可恢复约四分之一的情况。
tldr: 本文提出一个两层检测器，结合确定性检查和随机森林分类器，嵌入LangGraph状态机，有效识别和缓解本地编码大语言模型中的包名幻觉引发的slopsquatting供应链风险。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a two-layer detector combining deterministic checks and a Random Forest classifier, embedded in a LangGraph state machine, to effectively identify and mitigate slopsquatting supply chain risks caused by package name hallucinations in local coding LLMs.
